claim: Eukaryotic glycans are branched sugar oligomers attached to cell-surface proteins and lipids.
source: The synthesis of eukaryotic glycans – branched sugar oligomers attached to cell-surface proteins and lipids – is organized like a factory assembly line.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the abstract without specific experimental data or citations in this sentence.

claim: The synthesis of eukaryotic glycans is organized like a factory assembly line.
source: The synthesis of eukaryotic glycans – branched sugar oligomers attached to cell-surface proteins and lipids – is organized like a factory assembly line.
evidence: This is a conceptual framework presented by the authors based on the organization of glycan synthesis.

claim: Specific enzymes within successive compartments of the Golgi apparatus determine where new monomer building blocks are linked to the growing oligomer.
source: Specific enzymes within successive compartments of the Golgi apparatus determine where new monomer building blocks are linked to the growing oligomer.
evidence: This is established knowledge about Golgi function in glycan synthesis.

claim: Glycan synthesis enzymes act promiscuously and stochastically, causing microheterogeneity in the final oligomer products.
source: These enzymes act promiscuously and stochastically, causing microheterogeneity (molecule-to-molecule variability) in the final oligomer products.
evidence: This is presented as established knowledge about enzyme behavior.

claim: Glycan microheterogeneity is tightly controlled, with a given eukaryotic protein type typically associated with a narrow, specific glycan oligomer profile.
source: However, this variability is tightly controlled: a given eukaryotic protein type is typically associated with a narrow, specific glycan oligomer profile.
evidence: This is stated as an observed phenomenon in eukaryotic glycobiology.

claim: Cells can specifically synthesize a larger repertoire of glycan oligomers by partitioning promiscuous enzymes across multiple Golgi compartments.
source: We rigorously demonstrate that cells can specifically synthesize a larger repertoire of glycan oligomers by partitioning promiscuous enzymes across multiple Golgi compartments.
evidence: This is the main finding of the manuscript, demonstrated through mathematical theorems.

claim: Glycan microheterogeneity becomes unavoidable when the number of compartments is limited.
source: This places limits on biomolecular assembly: glycan microheterogeneity becomes unavoidable when the number of compartments is limited, or enzymes are excessively promiscuous.
evidence: This is a conclusion derived from the mathematical analysis presented in the manuscript.

claim: Glycan microheterogeneity becomes unavoidable when enzymes are excessively promiscuous.
source: This places limits on biomolecular assembly: glycan microheterogeneity becomes unavoidable when the number of compartments is limited, or enzymes are excessively promiscuous.
evidence: This is a conclusion derived from the mathematical analysis presented in the manuscript.

claim: Glycans are branched sugar oligomers covalently linked to proteins or lipids.
source: The surfaces of all living cells are decorated with information-rich oligosaccharide molecules known as glycans: branched sugar oligomers covalently linked to proteins or lipids (Varki et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to an established reference work.

claim: Glycans encode cell identity and mediate a variety of intercellular interactions.
source: Glycans encode cell identity and mediate a variety of intercellular interactions.
evidence: This is established knowledge about glycan function.

claim: Glycans play critical roles in development, species recognition, self-nonself discrimination, and host-pathogen coevolution.
source: They play critical roles in development, species recognition, self-nonself discrimination, and host-pathogen coevolution (Varki, 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to the literature.

claim: Glycans are composed of a small set of monosaccharide building block types and disaccharide bond types.
source: Glycans are composed of a small set of monosaccharide building block types (monomers) and disaccharide bond types (linkages in the branched glycan oligomer) (Adibekian et al., 2011; Figure 1A).
evidence: This is supported by a citation and reference to Figure 1A.

claim: Eukaryotic glycans are built by collections of glycosyltransferase (GTase) enzymes in the ER and Golgi apparatus.
source: Eukaryotic glycans are built by collections of glycosyltransferase (GTase) enzymes the ER and Golgi apparatus, a process known as glycosylation.
evidence: This is established knowledge about glycan biosynthesis.

claim: GTase enzymes are chemically precise but contextually sloppy.
source: GTase enzymes are chemically precise but contextually sloppy (Taniguchi and Honke, 2014; Biswas and Thattai, 2020): a given enzyme catalyzes a specific bond between a specific pair of monomer types, but can act promiscuously and stochastically on many oligomer types (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by citations and illustrated in Figure 1B.

claim: A given GTase enzyme catalyzes a specific bond between a specific pair of monomer types, but can act promiscuously and stochastically on many oligomer types.
source: GTase enzymes are chemically precise but contextually sloppy (Taniguchi and Honke, 2014; Biswas and Thattai, 2020): a given enzyme catalyzes a specific bond between a specific pair of monomer types, but can act promiscuously and stochastically on many oligomer types (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by citations and illustrated in Figure 1B.

claim: A single cell with a limited set of GTase enzymes can theoretically synthesize an astronomical array of oligomeric combinations.
source: As a consequence, even a single cell with a limited set of GTase enzymes can theoretically synthesize an astronomical array of oligomeric combinations (Cummings, 2009).
evidence: This is supported by a citation and represents an inference from enzyme promiscuity.

claim: The enzyme Fut2 requires the galactose acceptor to be linked to a GlcNAc root monomer.
source: The root-sensitive enzyme Fut2 requires the galactose acceptor to be linked to a GlcNAc root monomer.
evidence: This is stated as a property of the Fut2 enzyme, representing established knowledge about this specific enzyme.

claim: The enzyme GTB requires its galactose acceptor to have a fucose branch.
source: The branch-sensitive enzyme GTB requires its galactose acceptor to have a fucose branch.
evidence: This is stated as a property of the GTB enzyme, representing established knowledge about this specific enzyme.

claim: The enzyme β4GalNT1 can act on branched or un-branched galactose monomers.
source: The branch-insensitive enzyme β4GalNT1 can act on branched or un-branched galactose monomers.
evidence: This is stated as a property of the β4GalNT1 enzyme, representing established knowledge about this specific enzyme.

claim: Increased enzyme promiscuity leads to tandem repeat byproducts.
source: Increased enzyme promiscuity leads to tandem repeat byproducts.
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 1C and represents an inference from the model.

claim: Placing the context-free Fut2 enzyme in a separate compartment from branch-sensitive GTB restores specific synthesis of the B-antigen.
source: Placing the context-free Fut2 enzyme in a separate compartment from branch-sensitive GTB restores specific synthesis of the B-antigen.
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 1C as an example of how compartmentalization mitigates variability.

claim: Ideal root-sensitive enzymes can specifically synthesize any product in a single compartment.
source: Ideal root-sensitive enzymes can distinguish the position of every acceptor monomer in an oligomer, so they can specifically synthesize any product in a single compartment.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the mathematical analysis presented in the manuscript.

claim: Splitting branch-sensitive and context-free enzymes across multiple compartments increases the repertoire of oligomers they can specifically synthesize.
source: Branch-sensitive and context-free enzymes are more promiscuous; splitting such enzymes across multiple compartments increases the repertoire of oligomers they can specifically synthesize.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the mathematical analysis presented in the manuscript.

claim: Prokaryotic glycans are typically random heteropolymers.
source: The enormous potential for variability is exemplified by prokaryotic glycans, which are typically random heteropolymers (Varki et al., 2017, Chapter 21,22; Adibekian et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to the literature.

claim: Eukaryotic glycoproteins are typically associated with a narrow, specific set of glycan oligomers, referred to as protein's glycan profile.
source: In contrast, eukaryotic glycoproteins are typically associated with a narrow, specific set of glycan oligomers, referred to as protein's glycan profile (Varki et al., 2017, Chapter 1; Campbell et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to the literature.

claim: Specific protein glycan profiles are associated with distinct species.
source: The low variability of eukaryotic glycans is functionally relevant: specific protein glycan profiles are associated with distinct species (Hamako et al., 1993; Hård et al., 1992; Hokke et al., 1994), distinct individuals (as with ABO blood groups [Patenaude et al., 2002]) and distinct cell types in an individual [West et al., 2010]; and altered glycan profiles are implicated a variety of disorders (Freeze and Ng, 2011; Gill et al., 2013; Lo-Guidice et al., 1994).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to the literature.

claim: Specific protein glycan profiles are associated with distinct individuals, as with ABO blood groups.
source: The low variability of eukaryotic glycans is functionally relevant: specific protein glycan profiles are associated with distinct species (Hamako et al., 1993; Hård et al., 1992; Hokke et al., 1994), distinct individuals (as with ABO blood groups [Patenaude et al., 2002]) and distinct cell types in an individual [West et al., 2010]; and altered glycan profiles are implicated a variety of disorders (Freeze and Ng, 2011; Gill et al., 2013; Lo-Guidice et al., 1994).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to the literature.

claim: Specific protein glycan profiles are associated with distinct cell types in an individual.
source: The low variability of eukaryotic glycans is functionally relevant: specific protein glycan profiles are associated with distinct species (Hamako et al., 1993; Hård et al., 1992; Hokke et al., 1994), distinct individuals (as with ABO blood groups [Patenaude et al., 2002]) and distinct cell types in an individual [West et al., 2010]; and altered glycan profiles are implicated a variety of disorders (Freeze and Ng, 2011; Gill et al., 2013; Lo-Guidice et al., 1994).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to the literature.

claim: Altered glycan profiles are implicated in a variety of disorders.
source: The low variability of eukaryotic glycans is functionally relevant: specific protein glycan profiles are associated with distinct species (Hamako et al., 1993; Hård et al., 1992; Hokke et al., 1994), distinct individuals (as with ABO blood groups [Patenaude et al., 2002]) and distinct cell types in an individual [West et al., 2010]; and altered glycan profiles are implicated a variety of disorders (Freeze and Ng, 2011; Gill et al., 2013; Lo-Guidice et al., 1994).
evidence: This is supported by citations to the literature.

claim: Simulations suggest that the localization of enzymes within Golgi compartments plays a key role in controlling glycan variability.
source: Simulations suggest that the localization of enzymes within Golgi compartments plays a key role (Liu et al., 2008; Spahn and Lewis, 2014; Spahn et al., 2016; Fisher et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to simulation studies.

claim: The GTases Fut2 and GTB specifically synthesize the blood group B-antigen.
source: Consider the GTases Fut2 and GTB, which specifically synthesize the blood group B-antigen (Taniguchi and Honke, 2014, Chapter 44,47).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to the literature.

claim: Hypothetical promiscuous versions of Fut2 and GTB, if placed in a single compartment, generate variable tandem repeat oligomers as byproducts.
source: Hypothetical promiscuous versions of these enzymes, if placed in a single compartment, generate variable tandem repeat oligomers as byproducts (Figure 1C); specific synthesis of the B-antigen is restored when the promiscuous enzymes are placed in two separate compartments.
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 1C as a hypothetical example.

claim: Specific synthesis of the B-antigen is restored when promiscuous Fut2 and GTB enzymes are placed in two separate compartments.
source: Hypothetical promiscuous versions of these enzymes, if placed in a single compartment, generate variable tandem repeat oligomers as byproducts (Figure 1C); specific synthesis of the B-antigen is restored when the promiscuous enzymes are placed in two separate compartments.
evidence: This is demonstrated in Figure 1C as a hypothetical example.

claim: The synthesis of O-glycan oligomers begins in the Golgi apparatus when a root monomer is attached to a specific serine or threonine on a substrate protein.
source: The synthesis of O-glycan oligomers begins in the Golgi apparatus, when a root monomer is attached to a specific serine or threonine on a substrate protein.
evidence: This is established knowledge about O-glycan biosynthesis.

claim: The Golgi consists of an ordered series of compositionally distinct compartments.
source: The Golgi consists of an ordered series of compositionally distinct compartments (for example, cis, medial and trans cisternae).
evidence: This is established knowledge about Golgi structure.

claim: Each Golgi compartment contains a specific set of GTase enzymes responsible for growing an oligomer on a specific protein type.
source: Each compartment contains a specific set of GTase enzymes responsible for growing an oligomer on a specific protein type.
evidence: This is established knowledge about Golgi function.

claim: In the transport model, oligomers are ferried through successive Golgi compartments.
source: In the transport model, oligomers are ferried through successive compartments; in the maturation model, oligomers remain in place while the enzymatic composition of the compartment undergoes a rapid switch-like transition between successive states (Mani and Thattai, 2016; Pantazopoulou and Glick, 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations describing models of Golgi trafficking.

claim: In the maturation model, oligomers remain in place while the enzymatic composition of the compartment undergoes a rapid switch-like transition between successive states.
source: In the transport model, oligomers are ferried through successive compartments; in the maturation model, oligomers remain in place while the enzymatic composition of the compartment undergoes a rapid switch-like transition between successive states (Mani and Thattai, 2016; Pantazopoulou and Glick, 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations describing models of Golgi trafficking.

claim: Growing oligomers spend time within successive enzymatic compartment types under both transport and maturation models.
source: Under either scenario, whether transport or maturation, growing oligomers spend time within successive enzymatic compartment types.
evidence: This is an inference from the two models of Golgi trafficking.

claim: During each encounter with a GTase enzyme, the enzyme scans the oligomer for a site that matches a structural motif (the 'acceptor-substrate') and attaches a single free monomer (the 'donor-substrate') to that site.
source: During each such encounter, the enzyme scans the oligomer for a site that matches a structural motif (the 'acceptor-substrate') and attaches a single free monomer (the 'donor-substrate') to that site (Figure 1A; Liu et al., 2008; Moremen et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations and illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: A given GTase enzyme invariably catalyzes a glycosidic (C-O-C) linkage between specific carbons on a specific free donor monomer type and a specific acceptor monomer type within the acceptor-substrate.
source: A given GTase enzyme invariably catalyzes a glycosidic (C-O-C) linkage between specific carbons on a specific free donor monomer type and a specific acceptor monomer type within the acceptor-substrate (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is established knowledge about GTase specificity, illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: There are far fewer GTase enzymes than observed glycan oligomers in any given species.
source: First, there are far fewer GTase enzymes than observed glycan oligomers in any given species (Narimatsu et al., 2017); moreover, the same highly conserved enzymes are found across species with very distinct glycans (Kaneko et al., 2001; Figure 2).
evidence: This is supported by citations to the literature.

claim: The same highly conserved GTase enzymes are found across species with very distinct glycans.
source: First, there are far fewer GTase enzymes than observed glycan oligomers in any given species (Narimatsu et al., 2017); moreover, the same highly conserved enzymes are found across species with very distinct glycans (Kaneko et al., 2001; Figure 2).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to the literature and illustrated in Figure 2.

claim: By the pigeonhole principle, an individual GTase enzyme must be promiscuous and able to act on many distinct oligomer types.
source: Therefore, by the pigeonhole principle, an individual GTase enzyme must be promiscuous and able to act on many distinct oligomer types (Narimatsu et al., 2017).
evidence: This is an inference based on the pigeonhole principle, supported by a citation.

claim: There is a limit to the size of the motif any enzyme can recognize within an oligomer.
source: Second, although oligomers can be arbitrarily large, there is a limit to the size of the motif any enzyme can recognize within it.
evidence: This is a general principle about enzyme recognition capabilities.

claim: A given enzyme could act everywhere its recognition motif is found on an oligomer.
source: A given enzyme could act everywhere its recognition motif is found on an oligomer; the smaller the recognition motif, the more oligomers it will be found within, and the more promiscuous the enzyme (Blixt et al., 2008; Taniguchi and Honke, 2014; Biswas and Thattai, 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to the literature.

claim: The smaller the recognition motif, the more oligomers it will be found within, and the more promiscuous the enzyme.
source: A given enzyme could act everywhere its recognition motif is found on an oligomer; the smaller the recognition motif, the more oligomers it will be found within, and the more promiscuous the enzyme (Blixt et al., 2008; Taniguchi and Honke, 2014; Biswas and Thattai, 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to the literature and represents an inference about enzyme promiscuity.

claim: Context-free enzymes are maximally promiscuous.
source: Context-free enzymes are those whose acceptor-substrates are single monomers, no matter what branches or roots they are linked to. These enzymes are maximally promiscuous.
evidence: This is a definition and characterization provided by the authors.

claim: Ideal branch-sensitive enzymes are intermediate in promiscuity.
source: Ideal branch-sensitive enzymes are those whose acceptor-substrates are some acceptor monomer type having or lacking specific branches. These are intermediate in promiscuity.
evidence: This is a definition and characterization provided by the authors.

claim: Ideal root-sensitive enzymes are minimally promiscuous.
source: Ideal root-sensitive enzymes are those whose acceptor-substrates are some acceptor monomer type linked to a specific root chain. These enzymes can distinguish every monomer in an oligomer and are minimally promiscuous.
evidence: This is a definition and characterization provided by the authors.

claim: Chemical reactions within cells are necessarily stochastic, due to the low molecule numbers involved.
source: Chemical reactions within cells are necessarily stochastic, due to the low molecule numbers involved.
evidence: This is established knowledge about cellular biochemistry.

claim: While the growing oligomer is within a given compartment, the order in which it encounters the available GTase enzymes is equivalent to a Markov process of random sampling with replacement.
source: While the growing oligomer is within a given compartment, the order in which it encounters the available GTase enzymes is equivalent to a Markov process of random sampling with replacement, with randomly distributed time intervals between successive encounters (Gillespie, 1977).
evidence: This is a modeling assumption supported by a citation to stochastic simulation methods.

claim: O-glycan oligomers are not pruned, so their synthesis reactions are irreversible.
source: Since O-glycan oligomers are not pruned, these reactions are irreversible (Varki et al., 2017, Chapter 6).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to the literature.

claim: There are precisely three ways for variability to occur in assembly-line reactions: truncated, runaway, and divergent reactions.
source: We can show that there are precisely three ways for variability to occur (Appendix 2, Remark 1): truncated, runaway, and divergent reactions.
evidence: This is a mathematical result proven in the appendix.

claim: Each type of reaction variability corresponds to a specific output pattern that has been observed in real glycan datasets.
source: Each type of reaction variability corresponds to a specific output pattern that has been observed in real glycan datasets (Figure 2; Table 1; Varki et al., 2017, Chapter 1).
evidence: This is supported by reference to figures, tables, and citations.

claim: A truncated reaction causes intermediate oligomers to be produced as outputs.
source: A truncated reaction causes intermediate oligomers to be produced as outputs.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the mathematical analysis.

claim: Truncated reactions occur whenever the average waiting time for monomer addition is comparable to or greater than the compartment's residence time.
source: This occurs whenever the average waiting time for monomer addition (a quantity inversely proportional to enzyme concentrations) is comparable to or greater than the compartment's residence time (Appendix 2, Remark 1).
evidence: This is a mathematical result proven in the appendix.

claim: A runaway reaction is an infinite path in the reaction network, giving oligomers with arbitrary numbers of tandem repeats as outputs.
source: A runaway reaction is an infinite path in the reaction network, giving oligomers with arbitrary numbers of tandem repeats as outputs.
evidence: This is a definition provided by the authors.

claim: Ideal root-sensitive enzymes don't permit runaway reactions, since their acceptor monomers are at a fixed depth from the root.
source: Ideal root-sensitive enzymes don't permit runaway reactions, since their acceptor monomers are at a fixed depth from the root.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the mathematical analysis.

claim: A compartment contains a runaway reaction if and only if its linkage network contains one or more loops.
source: A compartment contains a runaway reaction if and only if its linkage network contains one or more loops (Appendix 2, Lemma 1), since each loop corresponds to a tandem repeat.
evidence: This is a mathematical theorem proven in the appendix.

claim: Branch-sensitive GTase enzymes can prevent linkage loops by using triggers.
source: Branch-sensitive GTase enzymes can prevent linkage loops by using triggers (branched acceptor-substrates that cannot be synthesized within the compartment from a single monomer; Figure 3D).
evidence: This is a conclusion from the mathematical analysis, illustrated in Figure 3D.

claim: A divergent reaction is a fork in the reaction network that never reconverges, with distinct paths leading to mutually exclusive oligomer fates as outputs.
source: A divergent reaction is a fork in the reaction network that never reconverges, with distinct paths leading to mutually exclusive oligomer fates as outputs.
evidence: This is a definition provided by the authors.

claim: If a fork does not reconverge, this implies that the action of one enzyme on an oligomer blocks the subsequent action of another.
source: If a fork does not reconverge this implies that the action of one enzyme on an oligomer blocks the subsequent action of another (Appendix 2, Lemma 2).
evidence: This is a mathematical result proven in the appendix.

claim: For root-sensitive and context-free enzymes, a non-reconverging fork can only occur if both enzymes compete to act on the same carbon of the same monomer (bidirectional acceptor block).
source: For root-sensitive and context-free enzymes, this can only occur if both enzymes compete to act on the same carbon of the same monomer (bidirectional acceptor block; Figure 3B).
evidence: This is a conclusion from the mathematical analysis, illustrated in Figure 3B.

claim: For branch-sensitive enzymes, a non-reconverging fork can occur if both enzymes have the same acceptor-substrate (bidirectional acceptor block) or if the acceptor-substrate of the first enzyme is on a branch of the acceptor-substrate of the second (unidirectional acceptor block).
source: For branch-sensitive enzymes, there are two ways this can occur: both enzymes have the same acceptor-substrate (bidirectional acceptor block; Figure 3B) or the acceptor-substrate of the first enzyme is on a branch of the acceptor-substrate of the second (unidirectional acceptor block; Figure 3B).
evidence: This is a conclusion from the mathematical analysis, illustrated in Figure 3B.

claim: Truncated reactions can be eliminated by requiring high enzyme concentrations.
source: We can eliminate truncated reactions by requiring high enzyme concentrations; we can eliminate linkage loops and acceptor blocks by removing certain enzymes from the reaction compartment (Figure 3C; Appendix 2, Lemma 3).
evidence: This is a conclusion from the mathematical analysis, illustrated in Figure 3C.

claim: Linkage loops and acceptor blocks can be eliminated by removing certain enzymes from the reaction compartment.
source: We can eliminate truncated reactions by requiring high enzyme concentrations; we can eliminate linkage loops and acceptor blocks by removing certain enzymes from the reaction compartment (Figure 3C; Appendix 2, Lemma 3).
evidence: This is a conclusion from the mathematical analysis, illustrated in Figure 3C.

claim: An 'algorithmic compartment' specifically synthesizes a corresponding unique output for each possible input.
source: These steps result in an 'algorithmic compartment': for each possible input, it specifically synthesizes a corresponding unique output.
evidence: This is a definition provided by the authors based on their mathematical analysis.

claim: A target oligomer can be specifically synthesized from an input oligomer if and only if it can be specifically synthesized from that input oligomer in a series of single-enzyme compartments.
source: A target oligomer can be specifically synthesized from an input oligomer if and only if it can be specifically synthesized from that input oligomer in a series of single-enzyme compartments.
evidence: This is Theorem 1, a mathematical result proven in the appendix.

claim: For ideal root-sensitive enzymes a single compartment is always sufficient, since every growth order to a given terminal oligomer is algorithmic.
source: For ideal root-sensitive enzymes a single compartment is always sufficient, since every growth order to a given terminal oligomer is algorithmic (Appendix 2, Lemma 4).
evidence: This is a mathematical result proven in the appendix.

claim: Certain oligomers can never be synthesized without byproducts, no matter how many compartments are allowed.
source: There are some situations in which glycan variability is unavoidable: certain oligomers can never be synthesized without byproducts, no matter how many compartments we allow.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the mathematical analysis.

claim: Eukaryotic glycan synthesis is an exquisite demonstration of template-free recipes to specifically encode diverse glycan oligomers.
source: Eukaryotic glycan synthesis is an exquisite demonstration of the same concept: re-configurable reaction networks act as template-free recipes to specifically encode diverse glycan oligomers.
evidence: This is an interpretation by the authors based on their analysis.

claim: When enzymes are promiscuous, the kinetics of distinct reactions cannot be independently regulated, leading to variability.
source: When enzymes are promiscuous, the kinetics of distinct reactions cannot be independently regulated, leading to variability (Biswas and Thattai, 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation.

claim: By splitting promiscuous enzymes across different Golgi compartments, glycan variability can be reduced or eliminated.
source: We have shown that, by splitting promiscuous enzymes across different Golgi compartments, this variability can be reduced or eliminated.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the manuscript, demonstrated through mathematical theorems.

claim: To synthesize oligomers without byproducts, cells must either decrease enzyme promiscuity, or increase the number of compartment types.
source: To synthesize oligomers without byproducts, cells must either decrease enzyme promiscuity, or increase the number of compartment types (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is a conclusion from the mathematical analysis, illustrated in Figure 1D.

claim: If all enzymes were highly selective, each with one specific substrate, a single compartment would suffice; but cells would require as many enzymes as oligomer types.
source: If all enzymes were highly selective, each with one specific substrate, a single compartment would suffice; but cells would require as many enzymes as oligomer types.
evidence: This is an inference about the trade-off between enzyme specificity and compartmentalization.

claim: An extensive system of membrane traffic proteins is required to maintain distinct Golgi compartments.
source: On the other hand, an extensive system of membrane traffic proteins is required to maintain distinct Golgi compartments (Pantazopoulou and Glick, 2019).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to the literature.

claim: Some GTase enzymes, such as those which synthesize the N-glycan oligomannose precursor in the ER, are highly selective and appear to act on just one or two oligomers.
source: Some GTase enzymes, such as those which synthesize the N-glycan oligomannose precursor in the ER, are highly selective and appear to act on just one or two oligomers; but most GTases are promiscuous, able to act on many oligomers or at many points on a single oligomer (Biswas and Thattai, 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to the literature.

claim: Most GTases are promiscuous, able to act on many oligomers or at many points on a single oligomer.
source: Some GTase enzymes, such as those which synthesize the N-glycan oligomannose precursor in the ER, are highly selective and appear to act on just one or two oligomers; but most GTases are promiscuous, able to act on many oligomers or at many points on a single oligomer (Biswas and Thattai, 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to the literature.

claim: Having multiple compartments is crucial for limiting glycan variability in real cells.
source: This means having multiple compartments is crucial for limiting glycan variability in real cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the analysis of enzyme promiscuity and compartmentalization.

claim: By redistributing enzymes within the Golgi, multicellular organisms can use the same set of enzymes to generate distinct glycan profiles in distinct cell types.
source: By redistributing enzymes within the Golgi, multicellular organisms can use the same set of enzymes to generate distinct glycan profiles in distinct cell types (Figure 2A; West et al., 2010; Fisher et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations and illustrated in Figure 2A.

claim: The rapid and reversible changes in glycan profiles seen during infection and inflammation are more consistent with changes in enzyme localization than changes in enzyme expression.
source: The rapid and reversible changes in glycan profiles seen during infection and inflammation (Varki et al., 2017, Chapter 46) are more consistent with changes in enzyme localization than changes in enzyme expression.
evidence: This is an inference supported by a citation about glycan changes during infection and inflammation.

claim: Changes in enzyme localization could facilitate rapid evolution of glycan profiles in the context of host-pathogen interactions and speciation.
source: Such changes could also facilitate rapid evolution of glycan profiles in the context of host-pathogen interactions and speciation (Watanabe et al., 2020; Varki et al., 2017, Chapter 20).
evidence: This is speculation supported by citations.

claim: Small errors in Golgi localization could be pathological.
source: But this also means small errors in Golgi localization could be pathological: glycan perturbations promoting tumor invasiveness appear to arise due to errors in enzyme localization, not mutations in the enzymes themselves (Gill et al., 2013; and congenital glycosylation disorders are often correlated with defects in Golgi structure (Freeze and Ng, 2011).
evidence: This is an inference supported by citations.

claim: Glycan perturbations promoting tumor invasiveness appear to arise due to errors in enzyme localization, not mutations in the enzymes themselves.
source: But this also means small errors in Golgi localization could be pathological: glycan perturbations promoting tumor invasiveness appear to arise due to errors in enzyme localization, not mutations in the enzymes themselves (Gill et al., 2013; and congenital glycosylation disorders are often correlated with defects in Golgi structure (Freeze and Ng, 2011).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to the literature.

claim: Congenital glycosylation disorders are often correlated with defects in Golgi structure.
source: But this also means small errors in Golgi localization could be pathological: glycan perturbations promoting tumor invasiveness appear to arise due to errors in enzyme localization, not mutations in the enzymes themselves (Gill et al., 2013; and congenital glycosylation disorders are often correlated with defects in Golgi structure (Freeze and Ng, 2011).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to the literature.

claim: The compartmental organization of the Golgi apparatus allows cells to control glycan synthesis despite enzymatic promiscuity.
source: Here, we have shown that the compartmental organization of the Golgi apparatus allows cells to control glycan synthesis despite enzymatic promiscuity, potentially explaining why this remarkable organelle is universally conserved across all extant eukaryotic lineages (Barlow et al., 2018).
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the manuscript, with a citation supporting the conservation of the Golgi.

claim: The Golgi apparatus is universally conserved across all extant eukaryotic lineages.
source: Here, we have shown that the compartmental organization of the Golgi apparatus allows cells to control glycan synthesis despite enzymatic promiscuity, potentially explaining why this remarkable organelle is universally conserved across all extant eukaryotic lineages (Barlow et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to the literature.

claim: The ability to generate narrow, specific glycan profiles would have been advantageous to early eukaryotes.
source: The ability to generate narrow, specific glycan profiles would have been advantageous to early eukaryotes (Wetzel et al., 2018), enabling the sophisticated intercellular interactions that underlie sex, cooperation and multicellularity.
evidence: This is speculation supported by a citation.

claim: Narrow, specific glycan profiles enable the sophisticated intercellular interactions that underlie sex, cooperation and multicellularity.
source: The ability to generate narrow, specific glycan profiles would have been advantageous to early eukaryotes (Wetzel et al., 2018), enabling the sophisticated intercellular interactions that underlie sex, cooperation and multicellularity.
evidence: This is speculation about the evolutionary advantages of controlled glycan synthesis.
